name: Starter thresholds — 18 coal-mine sensor parameters
about: One entry per CSV column. normal = typical range in normal operation (information only). warning / critical = the levels that raise CAUTION. worseWhen: higher | lower | detected | watch. Every entry here is PROVISIONAL (it can raise CAUTION, never UNSAFE) until you add a "verified" block after checking the numbers against your approved site standard. The verified Coal Mines Regulations 2017 rules (CH4, O2, CO2, flame, smoke) always apply on top and can give UNSAFE. See docs/site-thresholds.md.

CO_ppm.meaning: Toxic gas and the earliest sign of a spontaneous heating or fire. Fresh mine air holds only a few ppm. A steady rise means oxidising coal; hundreds of ppm means a serious heating or fire. IDLH is 1200 ppm.
CO_ppm.source: NIOSH REL 35 ppm (8-h TWA) and 200 ppm ceiling; IDLH 1200 ppm (NIOSH IDLH documentation for carbon monoxide)

CH4_vol_pct.meaning: Flammable gas released from coal. Explosive between about 5 and 15 % in air. Above 0.8 % more frequent checks are required; above 1.25 % anywhere, power must be cut off and the regulation is breached.
CH4_vol_pct.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 153(2)(c) and 169(1) (verified built-in rule)

O2_vol_pct.meaning: Fresh air is 20.9 %. A fall means oxygen is being used up by oxidising coal or fire, or displaced by other gases (blackdamp). Below 19 % persons must not work or pass.
O2_vol_pct.source: Warning 19.5 %: MSHA 30 CFR 75.321 minimum; critical 19 %: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 153(2)(b) (verified built-in rule)

CO2_vol_pct.meaning: Fresh air holds about 0.04 %. Rises with oxidation, fires, blasting fumes and poor ventilation. Above 0.5 % breaches the regulation where persons work or pass.
CO2_vol_pct.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 153(2)(b) (verified built-in rule)

H2_ppm.meaning: Normally absent (about 0.5 ppm in air). Appears when coal is very hot (well above 250 °C) and is itself flammable from 4 % (40 000 ppm). Any sustained hydrogen with rising CO points to an advanced heating or fire.
H2_ppm.source: Gas-detector practice: alarm at 10 % and 25 % of hydrogen's lower explosive limit (LEL 4 % vol = 40 000 ppm); hydrogen above 250 °C: NIOSH (CDC stacks 220814)

C2H4_ppm.meaning: Not present in fresh air. Released when coal heats beyond the early oxidation stage, so any ethylene confirms a developing heating. In the fire-gas sequence (CO, CO2, H2, ethylene, propylene, acetylene) gases after hydrogen indicate an active fire.
C2H4_ppm.source: Ray et al., J. Sci. Ind. Res. 63 (2004) 579-591, CIMFR Dhanbad: fire-gas progression

C2H2_ppm.meaning: Not present in fresh air. Last gas in the fire sequence; it appears only at very high temperature, so any acetylene means an active, intense fire.
C2H2_ppm.source: Ray et al., J. Sci. Ind. Res. 63 (2004) 579-591, CIMFR Dhanbad: fire-gas progression. Critical 0.5 ppm is a starting value (above detector noise)

Coal_Seam_Temp_C.meaning: Undisturbed seams in Indian mines are usually 25-40 °C. Coal that warms past about 70-80 °C can run away to self-ignition; above 250 °C the heating is critical.
Coal_Seam_Temp_C.source: Thermal runaway from 70-80 °C in adiabatic tests and critical stage above 250 °C (NIOSH, CDC stacks 220814). Warning 50 °C is a starting value

Airway_Temp_C.meaning: Heat stress and a sign of a heating upstream. The regulation limits WET-bulb temperature (30.5 °C needs 1 m/s air, 33.5 °C maximum); dry-bulb is always at or above wet-bulb, so using the same numbers here is conservative.
Airway_Temp_C.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 153(2)(d) wet-bulb limits, applied conservatively to a dry-bulb reading

Thermal_IR_Max_C.description: Hottest surface seen by the thermal (IR) camera
Thermal_IR_Max_C.meaning: Hot spots on coal faces, belts, rollers or equipment. Equipment for coal mines must stay below 150 °C where coal dust can settle on it; coal surfaces above about 70 °C can self-heat.
Thermal_IR_Max_C.source: IEC 60079-0 Group I maximum surface temperature 150 °C where coal dust can form a layer; warning 70 °C matches the coal self-heating range

Air_Velocity_m_s.meaning: Ventilation keeps gas diluted and carries heat away. Too slow and methane or heat builds up. CMR asks at least 1 m/s where wet-bulb exceeds 30.5 °C and at least 30 m/min (0.5 m/s) at the outbye connection from a face.
Air_Velocity_m_s.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 153(2)(d) (1 m/s) and Reg. 160 table (30 m/min); applied at any sensor location as a starting value

Barometric_Pressure_kPa.meaning: The absolute value is not a hazard. A sudden FALL draws methane and fire gases out of goaves and sealed areas, so watch the trend chart and report any unusual change.
Barometric_Pressure_kPa.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 46(1)(o): report any unusual change (no numeric limit)

Smoke_Obscuration_pct.description: Smoke obscuration (how much smoke blocks the sensor's light path)
Smoke_Obscuration_pct.meaning: Clean air reads near 0 %. Any persistent smoke is a sign of fire (Reg. 138: on the appearance of smoke, act and withdraw persons). Set these to your sensor maker's alarm levels.
Smoke_Obscuration_pct.source: Starting values; replace with your smoke sensor's alarm settings. Context: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 138(1)

Grahams_Ratio.description: Graham's ratio (CO formed / O2 absorbed × 100, in %)
Grahams_Ratio.meaning: Best single indicator of spontaneous heating. 0.4 % or less is normal; 0.5 % needs a thorough check; 1 % indicates heating; 2 % serious heating approaching fire; 3 % and above an active fire. Unreliable when the oxygen deficiency is under 0.3 %.
Grahams_Ratio.source: Ray et al., J. Sci. Ind. Res. 63 (2004) 579-591, CIMFR Dhanbad: Graham's ratio thumb rule

Trickett_Ratio.description: Jones-Trickett ratio ((CO2 + 0.75 CO − 0.25 H2) / O2 absorbed)
Trickett_Ratio.meaning: Tells WHAT is burning, not how dangerous it is: 0.4-0.5 methane; 0.5-1.0 coal, oil or conveyor belt; 0.9-1.6 timber. A value above 1.6 fits no fuel and usually means a bad sample or sensor, so check the gas readings.
Trickett_Ratio.source: Ray et al., J. Sci. Ind. Res. 63 (2004) 579-591, CIMFR Dhanbad: Jones and Trickett fuel ranges (upper end 1.6)

Explosion_Risk_Index.description: Explosion risk index (from your monitoring system)
Explosion_Risk_Index.meaning: ASSUMED scale: 0 = not explosive, 1 = could become explosive if mixed with air, 2 = explosive mixture (Coward-diagram style). Confirm what your system's numbers mean and edit these levels.
Explosion_Risk_Index.source: Assumed 0/1/2 scale; confirm with the system that produces this index

YOLO_Flame_Detected.description: Flame seen by the camera AI (1 = yes, 0 = no)
YOLO_Flame_Detected.meaning: Any detection is a possible fire: follow the fire procedure and have a competent person confirm.
YOLO_Flame_Detected.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 138(1) (verified built-in rule)

YOLO_Smoke_Detected.description: Smoke seen by the camera AI (1 = yes, 0 = no)
YOLO_Smoke_Detected.meaning: Any detection is a possible fire: follow the fire procedure and have a competent person confirm.
YOLO_Smoke_Detected.source: Coal Mines Regulations 2017, Reg. 138(1) (verified built-in rule)
